ticket.title: Cross-ledger edges: uuid identity plus a repository locator, never a copy
ticket.description:
An edge carries the target uuid for identity and a repo:key locator for finding and rendering it. The contract already documents target_ticket_key and target_repo for cross-repository rendering and 106 of 123 edge events populate them, but nothing consumes them. Live cross-ledger edges: parent_epic 12, related_to 15, blocked_by 7; 12 run from a member to a root epic, which is the case a solo clone cannot resolve and must not resolve by copying the target, since copying is how GB-79 produced two live copies of one task. Rendering: repository unreachable means show the key with its repository and no link; reachable means resolve by uuid.

CONFIRMED SCOPE 2026-11-08, from the consumer sweep that followed SP-36.

This ticket owns three pieces, not one:
  1. schema: task_edges gains target_ticket_key and target_repo (index/schema.rs), because the table currently
     stores task_id, kind, target_id and drops the two fields 106 of 123 edge events already carry;
  2. insert path: index::insert_task_record must write them, or the columns stay empty and the schema change
     buys nothing;
  3. rendering: a member-only view must show a cross-repository target as its key plus repository rather than
     a bare uuid. Consumers: benchwork DagBoard and the workspace rollup.

The live numbers that justify it: 7 blocked_by, 15 related_to, 12 parent_epic cross-ledger edges, of which 12
run from a member to a root epic - the case a single checkout cannot resolve and must not resolve by copying the
target (GB-79).
acceptance_criteria: a benchwork clone with no root checkout renders its parent as a key with a repository, not a uuid; no edge handler writes a copy of the target task

TWO OF THREE DONE 2026-11-08 (commit 60309bb).

Schema and insert path are in: task_edges carries target_ticket_key and target_repo, insert_task_record writes
them, and init_schema upgrades an index built before they existed - the case that matters, because
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cannot alter a table and every existing index.sqlite would otherwise have kept three
columns and dropped the locator on every rebuild, silently.

place.

Remaining: the rendering, so a consumer shows SP-29 (gaugeblock) instead of a uuid. Consumer-side, and it belongs
with whoever draws the graph - benchwork's DagBoard is the named one.

CONSUMER GEOGRAPHY VERIFIED 2026-11-08, for the rendering piece (pieces 1 and 2, schema and insert, are already done).

  crates/benchwork-core/src/model/dag.rs       52 lines - `DagQuery`, `DagView`, `DagStats`. No edge label field, so
                                               nothing here is a rendering decision yet.
  crates/benchwork-core/src/dag_service/query.rs  188 lines - the service that builds a view.
  crates/benchwork-core/src/dag_service/routing.rs - where links are created, and where `target_id` is resolved before
                                               insert.

WHAT A GREP FOR `unresolved | Unknown | dangling` FOUND IN query.rs: nothing. There is no representation of an edge whose
target this checkout cannot resolve - not a placeholder, not a warning, not a count. So the rendering piece is not a
matter of changing a format string from uuid to `KEY (repo)`; the state has no shape in the view at all, and the case the
ticket calls out (12 edges from a member to a root epic, unresolvable in a solo clone) is currently silent.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE WORK: the first step is to give the state a name in `DagView` - an edge target that is known by
locator and not by identity - and only then to decide how it renders. Formatting before the state exists would put
`KEY (repo)` in front of a reader while leaving `DagStats` unable to report that some edges were not resolved, which is
the number an operator actually needs when looking at a graph that is missing twelve edges.

STOPPED THERE deliberately: this is now a model change in a second repository, not a rendering tweak, and it needs the
same gate as any other.
